items.title: What investors 'really' need to see from Oracle earnings this week
items.summary: Oracle (ORCL) is reporting quarterly earnings results on Thursday. Bloomberg Intelligence senior technology credit analyst Robert Schiffman shares what investors should be keeping an eye on in the earnings print, especially from a debt-issuance perspective.

items.title: Uber Stock Falls As Wall Street Sizes Up Tesla's Cybercab Rollout
items.summary: Uber stock fell Tuesday as investors continued to debate the competitive threat of Tesla's Cybercab plans.

items.title: Cloud Capex to Cash: AWS Wins This Way, Alphabet Wins Another Way
items.summary: AWS and Google Cloud are both burning through tens of billions in capex every quarter, but only one is converting that spending into free cash flow at hyperscale margins right now. Which model actually wins when the 2027 capacity cliff arrives?

items.title: Google’s revived nuclear power plant gets $1.9B loan from US government
items.summary: Google said it would bring an Iowa nuclear power plant back from the dead. Now, the plant's owner is getting a $1.9B loan from the U.S. Energy Department.

items.title: Uber Technologies Poised to Benefit From Long-Term Trend for Autonomous Vehicles, Wedbush Says
items.summary: Uber Technologies (UBER) will benefit from the long-term trend for autonomous vehicles, Wedbush said

items.title: Could Apple Face a $17 Billion Child Safety Settlement Like Meta?
items.summary: West Virginia's attorney general just called Meta's $17 billion child safety settlement a smart business move, then pointed directly at Apple as the next target. What he says Apple's iCloud is hiding could upend the privacy brand Tim Cook spent a decade building.

items.title: Beyond Social: Meta Is Buying the Future of Compute So I’m Buying It
items.summary: Meta is quietly assembling one of the largest AI compute empires on the planet, and the funding source hiding in plain sight changes everything about how you should value this stock.

items.title: Alphabet Stock Is Pulling Back From Its High. Here’s Why I’d Buy the Dip.
items.summary: Alphabet just posted blowout earnings and yet the stock has shed more than 10% from its peak, leaving investors caught between soaring Cloud growth and a balance sheet that suddenly looks very different from a year ago.
